title: Mapping-space fibers over an edge are mapping spaces in the edge pullback
statement:
Use simplicial sets, quasicategories, functor simplicial sets $\operatorname{Fun}(K,-)$, constant-diagram maps $\Delta_K$, coherent composition, right-pinched mapping spaces, Kan complexes, homotopy fibers and weak homotopy equivalences as in [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], and inner fibrations as in [def-coef-infinity-fibrations]. A Kan fibration is a simplicial map with the right lifting property against every horn inclusion $\Lambda_k^n\hookrightarrow\Delta^n$, $n\geq1$, $0\leq k\leq n$. Let $p:E\to B$ be an inner fibration between quasicategories, and let $f:b\to s$ be an edge of $B$ (possibly degenerate). Let $E_f=E\times_{B,f}\Delta^1$ be the degreewise pullback, with projections $j:E_f\to E$ and $p_f:E_f\to\Delta^1$. Its fibers over $0$ and $1$ are $E_b=E\times_B\{b\}$ and $E_s=E\times_B\{s\}$, and an object $y$ of one of them is written $(y,0)$, respectively $(y,1)$, in $E_f$. Let $K$ be a small simplicial set, possibly empty, and let $A:K\to E_b$ and $Z:K\to E_s$ be diagrams. Write $p_K:\operatorname{Fun}(K,E)\to\operatorname{Fun}(K,B)$ for postcomposition with $p$. Then:

(1) $p_K$ is an inner fibration between quasicategories, $E_f$ and $\operatorname{Fun}(K,E_f)$ are quasicategories, and $\operatorname{Fun}(K,E_f)=\operatorname{Fun}(K,E)\times_{\operatorname{Fun}(K,B)}\operatorname{Fun}(K,\Delta^1)$ degreewise.

(2) $\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Fun}(K,\Delta^1)}(\Delta_K0,\Delta_K1)$ has exactly one simplex in each degree. Postcomposition with $f$ carries it to the constant vertex $\Delta_Kf$ of $\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Fun}(K,B)}(\Delta_Kb,\Delta_Ks)$ and its degeneracies.

(3) The map $\pi:\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Fun}(K,E)}(A,Z)\to\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Fun}(K,B)}(\Delta_Kb,\Delta_Ks)$ induced by $p_K$ is a Kan fibration between Kan complexes. Postcomposition with $j$ is an isomorphism of simplicial sets from $\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Fun}(K,E_f)}((A,0),(Z,1))$ onto the strict fiber $\pi^{-1}(\Delta_Kf)$. Followed by the constant-path inclusion of that strict fiber into $\operatorname{hofib}_{\Delta_Kf}(\pi)$, it gives a weak homotopy equivalence
$$\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Fun}(K,E_f)}((A,0),(Z,1))\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }\operatorname{hofib}_{\Delta_Kf}\bigl(\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Fun}(K,E)}(A,Z)\to\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Fun}(K,B)}(\Delta_Kb,\Delta_Ks)\bigr).$$

(4) These equivalences are induced by the simplicial map $j$, and they are natural. They commute with restriction along any simplicial map $L\to K$ and with the constant-diagram maps $\Delta_K$. They also commute with coherent precomposition by an edge of $\operatorname{Fun}(K,E_b)$ and with coherent postcomposition by an edge of $\operatorname{Fun}(K,E_s)$, when the composite is formed in $\operatorname{Fun}(K,E_f)$ and its image under $j$ is taken as the composite in $\operatorname{Fun}(K,E)$. Such an image lies over the degenerate composite with $\Delta_Kf$ in $\operatorname{Fun}(K,B)$.

For $K=\Delta^0$ this says that, for $x\in E_b$ and $z\in E_s$, $\operatorname{Map}_E(x,z)\to\operatorname{Map}_B(b,s)$ is a Kan fibration whose fiber over $f$ is $\operatorname{Map}_{E_f}((x,0),(z,1))$, equivalent to the homotopy fiber over $f$. No cocartesian or cartesian edge of $p$ is assumed.

source.place: Higher Topos Theory, proof of Proposition 4.3.1.10 (printed pp. 265-266), the reduction of the relative mapping-space test to the pullback of p along one edge; Corollary 2.3.2.5 for inner exponentiation and Lemma 2.4.4.1 for the Kan fibration. HTT is not archived under literature/ (WANTED by the item's report). The statement was checked directly from the definitions by the maintainer reader.

proof.text: First establish the exponentiation assertion of (1). A lifting square for $p_K$ against $\Lambda_i^n\hookrightarrow\Delta^n$ is, by the displayed definition of $\operatorname{Fun}$, a lifting square for $p$ against $K\times\Lambda_i^n\hookrightarrow K\times\Delta^n$. The inner horn inclusion is inner anodyne: every inner fibration lifts it by definition. Apply [lem-coef-inner-anodyne-pushout-product] to this inclusion and $\varnothing\hookrightarrow K$; its pushout-product, after swapping factors, is exactly this product inclusion, so $p$ supplies the required lift. Thus $p_K$ is inner. The identical argument for $Q\to\Delta^0$, where $Q$ is any quasicategory, shows that $\operatorname{Fun}(K,Q)$ is a quasicategory: an inner horn there is adjoint to a product horn in $Q$. Apply this to $Q=E,B$. No quasicategory condition on $K$ was used.

source.place: Agent expansion of the middle mapping-complex comparison, paragraph 2: inner exponentiation needed for its mapping-space model; compare HTT 2.3.2.4-5.

proof.text: The simplicial set $\Delta^1$ is a quasicategory directly: a simplex in it is a nondecreasing string of zeros and ones; the consecutive edges of an inner horn force its vertex string to be nondecreasing, and that string supplies its filler. In a horn lifting square for $p_f:E_f\to\Delta^1$, the given map to $\Delta^1$ and its composite with $f$ give a lifting square for $p$. Pair its filler with the given simplex of $\Delta^1$ to get a filler for $p_f$. Consequently $p_f$ is inner. To fill an inner horn in $E_f$, first fill its projection in $\Delta^1$, then lift this filler by $p_f$. This proves that $E_f$ is a quasicategory. Apply the exponentiation argument of step 1 to $E_f$ and $\Delta^1$ to obtain their functor quasicategories.

source.place: Agent degreewise lifting argument for the edge-pullback reduction supporting paragraph 2.

proof.text: For each $n$, a map $K\times\Delta^n\to E_f$ is precisely a pair $(u,v)$ of maps to $E$ and $\Delta^1$ with $p u=f v$. This follows by taking the two coordinates in the defining degreewise pullback; conversely such a pair is a simplicial map into it because every operator acts coordinatewise. Restricting on $\Delta^n$ restricts both coordinates. This gives the asserted degreewise identification of functor simplicial sets in (1), including its projections.

source.place: Agent coordinate calculation for paragraph 2: functor simplicial sets preserve this specified pullback.

proof.text: Put $q_n:\Delta^{n+1}\to\Delta^1$ for the monotone map sending $0,\ldots,n$ to $0$ and $n+1$ to $1$. An $n$-simplex of the mapping space in (2) is a map $v:K\times\Delta^{n+1}\to\Delta^1$ equal to $0$ on $K\times\Delta^{\{0,\ldots,n\}}$ and $1$ on $K\times\{n+1\}$. These conditions prescribe every vertex value. Every simplex of $\Delta^1$ is uniquely determined by its ordered vertices, so they force $v=q_n\operatorname{pr}_{\Delta^{n+1}}$. This formula supplies such a map and is preserved by all right-pinched operators. If $K=\varnothing$, the domain is empty and again there is exactly one map. Thus this mapping simplicial set is the one-point simplicial set. Composing its displayed simplex with $f$ gives precisely the $n$-fold degenerate simplex of the vertex $\Delta_K f$.

source.place: Agent calculation of the base mapping-space singleton in the edge-pullback comparison, paragraph 2.

proof.text: Since $p_K$ is inner between quasicategories by step 1, [lem-coef-infinity-inner-mapping-fiber] applied to its vertices $A,Z$ proves that $\pi$ is a Kan fibration. To check that its source and target are Kan as well, apply that same cited statement to $Q\to\Delta^0$ for $Q=\operatorname{Fun}(K,E),\operatorname{Fun}(K,B)$: this map is inner by the quasicategory horn condition, and the mapping space of the terminal quasicategory has one simplex in each degree. Thus its conclusion is exactly the Kan condition for each of the two mapping spaces. The same reasoning applies to the mapping space in $\operatorname{Fun}(K,E_f)$.

source.place: Agent application of the existing general mapping-space fibration theorem in paragraph 2; compare HTT 2.4.4.1.

proof.text: In degree $n$, use step 3 to write a simplex of $\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Fun}(K,E_f)}((A,0),(Z,1))$ as a pair $(u,v)$ on $K\times\Delta^{n+1}$. The endpoint restrictions on $u$ are $A\operatorname{pr}_K$ on the entire initial face and $Z$ on the last vertex, so $u$ is an $n$-simplex of $\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Fun}(K,E)}(A,Z)$. Step 4 forces $v=q_n\operatorname{pr}$. The remaining pullback equation is therefore $p u=fq_n\operatorname{pr}$, exactly the equation that $\pi(u)$ be the $n$-fold degeneracy of $\Delta_K f$. Conversely a simplex $u$ satisfying this equation has the unique preimage $(u,q_n\operatorname{pr})$. Both assignments commute with all operators because $q_n\circ\alpha^+=q_m$ for the last-vertex extension $\alpha^+:[m+1]\to[n+1]$. This proves the strict-fiber isomorphism of (3); its forward map is precisely postcomposition with $j$.

source.place: Agent explicit inverse for the edge-pullback fiber identification supporting paragraph 2.

proof.text: Set $U=\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Fun}(K,E)}(A,Z)$ and $W=\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Fun}(K,B)}(\Delta_K b,\Delta_K s)$. Step 5 verifies that $U,W$ are Kan and $u=\pi:U\to W$ is a Kan fibration. Apply [lem-coef-kan-pullback-path-comparison] with $V=\Delta^0$ and $v$ the vertex $\Delta_K f$. Its strict pullback is $\pi^{-1}(\Delta_K f)$ and its path pullback is exactly the homotopy fiber specified in the statement. Its actual comparison inserts the constant path; hence composing it with the isomorphism in step 6 gives exactly the asserted weak homotopy equivalence, with the requested direction and map.

source.place: Agent application of the general constant-path comparison in paragraph 2; Kerodon 0329 supplies this general theorem, not a Stacks tag.

proof.text: For a map $a:L\to K$, restriction sends $u$ to $u(a\times\mathrm{id})$. It sends the unique coordinate $q_n\operatorname{pr}$ of step 6 to the same coordinate on $L\times\Delta^{n+1}$, and sends the base vertex to $\Delta_L f$. Thus the forward and inverse strict-fiber maps commute with restriction. On homotopy fibers the induced map is $(u,\gamma)\mapsto(a^*u,a^*\gamma)$; the constant path at $\Delta_K f$ restricts to the constant path at $\Delta_L f$. This proves the same commutation for the weak equivalences. Taking $K\to\Delta^0$ as the restriction map gives the claimed compatibility with $\Delta_K$. Taking $K=\Delta^0$ gives the last paragraph of the statement, since $\operatorname{Fun}(\Delta^0,Q)=Q$ degreewise.

source.place: Agent naturality of the specified maps in paragraph 2: restriction and constant diagrams.

proof.text: For coherent composition use the triangle spaces $V$ and edge restrictions $\theta,\ell$ of [lem-coef-infinity-mapping-composition]. Applied in the two functor quasicategories, $j$ sends each triangle and all its parameter simplices to its image and commutes with $\theta$ and $\ell$, since these are restrictions. The right-pinch inclusions are natural by [lem-coef-infinity-pinch-comparison]; hence the formula for the canonical composition class in the former citation commutes with $j$ (invert the commuting $[\theta]$ in the homotopy category). In particular this applies to precomposition by an edge $A'\to A$ in $\operatorname{Fun}(K,E_b)$ and postcomposition by an edge $Z\to Z'$ in $\operatorname{Fun}(K,E_s)$. For any parameter simplex of a triangle in $\operatorname{Fun}(K,E_f)$, its base map $K\times\Delta^2\times\Delta^n\to\Delta^1$ has vertex labels $001$ for precomposition and $011$ for postcomposition. As in step 4, vertices determine every simplex of $\Delta^1$, so it is the projection followed by that vertex word. Its $02$ edge is therefore $q_0$, and its image under $f$ is constant in the parameter at $\Delta_K f$. For a higher string replace $\Delta^2$ by $\Delta^r$: the base is again the projection followed by its fixed monotone vertex word, and restricting to any face restricts that word. Thus every supplied higher witness has image over the prescribed degeneracies, and each output remains in the strict fiber of step 6. On each such output simplex $u$, the comparison is $(j_*u,\operatorname{const}_{\Delta_K f})$; restricting a witness restricts $j_*u$ and preserves this constant path. This proves the coherent compatibility in the path model. This is the statement's convention of taking the image of the chosen composite; no functor-independent strict choice of composition is needed. If $K$ is empty all these simplicial sets and maps are terminal.

source.place: Agent compatibility with chosen coherent composites for paragraph 2; Kerodon 01PF and the existing natural right-pinch comparison specify the composition convention.
